questions.question: What does display actually control?
questions.answer: It sets the element's outer box type (block, inline, inline-block) and often its inner layout mode (flex, grid, contents, none). It determines whether a box exists and how children participate in layout.

questions.question: Why do width and height fail on inline elements?
questions.answer: Inline boxes are sized by their content and line layout, so width/height are ignored. Use inline-block or a flex/grid item when you need both inline flow and explicit sizing.

questions.question: Compare display:none, visibility:hidden, and opacity:0.
questions.answer: display:none removes the box, space, accessibility, and clicks. visibility:hidden keeps layout space but removes paint, accessibility, and clicks. opacity:0 keeps space and accessibility and remains clickable.

questions.question: What is the difference between overflow:auto, hidden, and clip?
questions.answer: auto adds scrollbars only when needed. hidden clips overflow and can scroll programmatically but shows no scrollbar. clip cuts off overflow and cannot scroll.

questions.question: What does object-fit do, and when do you use it?
questions.answer: It controls how replaced content (img/video) fills its box: cover crops to fill, contain fits entirely, fill stretches. Use it when fixed dimensions would otherwise distort media.

questions.question: Create a circular avatar that crops a non-square image without distortion.
Why is opacity:0 dangerous for a hidden menu?
questions.answer: The element still occupies space, is announced by screen readers, and remains clickable/focusable, so users can tab into invisible controls. Use visibility:hidden, display:none, or remove it from the DOM.

questions.question: Why does display:contents sometimes break accessibility?
questions.answer: It removes the element's box, so its own background/border disappear and certain elements (notably buttons) can lose their semantic role in some browsers. Use it only for pure wrappers and test with assistive tech.
